Super Governance Opportunity:

> *<https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/miri/5d13ba07-8fbf-4f46-aa1b-9000a7d1dc3f|MIRI is hiring Policy Advisors> to help us build our DC policy efforts*
> MIRI is a nonprofit that has been working on avoiding catastrophic outcomes from advanced AI for over 20 years. After doing technical research for much of that time, MIRI pivoted to focusing on raising awareness of the threat and identifying policy responses. Now, the danger seems close. We’re aiming to significantly ramp up our engagement with the U.S. Federal Government in the coming weeks, as we see major gaps and opportunities. There is movement on serious AI policy, including growing support for a ban on superintelligence, yet much more work is needed.

The *California Governor's Office of Emergency Services (Cal OES)* is hiring 2+ Senior AI Fellows and a Cyber Policy Strategy Planner. You'll work with myself and <@U04G7R6ECMC> (formerly at METR) on frontier AI policy implementation. You'll work on topics like internal-risk assessments from frontier AI companies, AI incident reporting and response, minimum safety and security standards, AI kill switches, and/or AI cyber defense. Cal OES leadership sees emergency preparedness against AI threats like rogue AI as a major priority, so you'll be empowered to do great things.

If interested, message me and email <mailto:implementation@secureaiproject.org|implementation@secureaiproject.org> (not affiliated with the role), and apply to roles from <http://linktr.ee/caloes.ai|http://linktr.ee/caloes.ai> within the next week or two.

We have a stealth opportunity.  Let me know if interested.
> :lock: Hiring: new AI security research lab (stealth)
>  Recursive self-improvement may be the most consequential technology we have ever faced, and it is also the largest unprotected attack surface in AI. A new nonprofit lab in Berkeley is building the team to secure it, across threat modeling, containment, monitoring and more.
>  Hiring a wide range of roles: Research Lead, MTS, Generalist, Research Intern (3-6 months). They’re looking for folks with a security mindset, self-directed, with a background in AI safety and/or security. Berkeley/SF preferred, remote for strong fits. Competitive pay.
>  Interested? DM me and I’ll connect you :raised_hands:

I just joined MITRE’s Trustworthy and Secure AI department and they are still hiring: <https://careers.mitre.org/us/en/job/R116626/AI-Security-Engineer|careers.mitre.org/us/en/…/AI-Security-Engineer>

They do things like securing AI, AI redteaming, evaluations, are familiar with mech interp. Lmk if you have any questions or want a referral. (If you want a referral maybe don’t create an account on the MITRE website yet.)

More details on that very cool Transluce job!
> *Technical Program Manager, Transluce (San Francisco)*
> Transluce is a nonprofit AI evaluation lab that works with frontier AI developers and governments. We recently uncovered an <https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/23/technology/openai-ai-breach-australia.html|OpenAI agent breaking into an Australian government website>, and we’re preparing multi-week, on-premise embedded evaluations with frontier AI labs.
> We’re hiring a <https://jobs.gem.com/transluce/am9icG9zdDoab9RnElyj4J7icPcuIhK_|Technical Program Manager> to own such engagements end to end: scoping and negotiating terms, steering the technical team through the evaluation, and presenting findings to partners and the public.
> It’s a high-agency role; you’d be establishing the practice of embedded evaluations as you go. It suits someone who has built from zero to one in a fast-moving environment, excels at managing external partners, and understands frontier AI evaluations well enough to engage substantively with technical staff.
> San Francisco based, visa sponsorship available, $250k to $350k plus bonus and benefits. Questions about the role or process: <mailto:amin@transluce.org|amin@transluce.org>.
